A one-line algebra makes it worse. Write R = f(img) + e, so Y = (R + f_hat)/2 and E[Y|img] ≈ f. The gate's gain is the report half's own noise averaging out, which a student gets anyway. HELD.
(2) I tried to call (b) a forced, disclosed limitation. It was: dread_soft has no gold rows (AUDIT:141), and the project discounted the gain and priced the LB at +0.005-0.010 (archive :620-621, :652). So (b) is a measurement weakness, not a hidden error. WEAKENED.
(3) I tried to argue that same-label k-fold teachers still help. They can, through (i) reduced memorisation of label noise, since OOF predictions are independent of each study's own noise, and (ii) a different inductive bias. Both are second-order. The LB (~0 to +0.005), gold (0.911 vs 0.912; 0.9192 vs 0.9187) and OOF correlations all agree. (c) HELD as 'mostly'.
(4) I tried to say (d) breaks rule 3, since the 691 cannot judge teachers. Not quite: on fixed dread_soft labels the 691 is a valid strength comparison (0.832 vs dread 0.844), and gold agrees. fix:
1. Keep same-label teacher rounds closed. WIN-PLAN already did this (no round-2 Ortho folds, saving ~20-37 quota-h).
2. Write a standing gate rule. Any label or target change is gated against the incumbent model's own gold read, never against the report alone. Targets that contain an image model's output cannot be gated on gold at all, because the student only learns E[target|image]; such targets go straight to an LB student or are dropped.
3. Do not let the round-1 targets ride into the finals by default. The Ortho final now training uses them plus the confidence weight. Decide them by the planned T1 (teacher targets, current loss) vs T2 (dread_soft, frontier loss) forced choice, both all-data, on the LB.
4. Is any teacher worth running toward 0.965? A teacher pays only if it carries information the student cannot get from its own labels. In-licence there is none:
   - Different labels: a criteria-graded API read (L3) should train the student directly. A teacher adds nothing.
   - External images: NYU and OAI are licence-excluded from finals, and NYU pseudo-knees measured null (P 0.75).
   - Gold: 58 studies is too few to train on, and it is the only image-graded check.
   - In-domain unlabelled images: none exist; test is hidden.
   - A stronger-input teacher distilled into a weaker-input student: the student still only learns E[target | its own input].
   So the route is closed. Put its budget into grader-side label information (L3, after L9 provenance) and the exact-copy/all-data recipe arms.

(1) Was it deliberate? Yes. It is documented as a deliberate difference (train_windows.py:27,31-32). (3) Is the cost on dread_soft overstated? Largely yes. Most dread_soft cells sit at levels weighted 0.70–0.925, so the spread is only about 1.3× for Effusion and Baker's. That weakens the dread_soft half of the claim.

(4) Does it mute the teacher's corrections? Only partly. BCE is linear in the target, so with or without the weight the report's confident wrong label is dropped from a conflict cell. The weight makes the conflict cell low-influence, which is an agreement filter, much like FixMatch/UPS-style masking of uncertain pseudo-labels, a standard and often helpful practice. What it really removes is the 3–4× stronger pull toward the middle that the gold gate validated. The direction of the effect is therefore genuinely uncertain.

refutation_attempts: (1) Was it a deliberate, defensible choice? Partly yes. k=12 is copied from the frontier's script (MODEL.md:24, train_windows.py:19-20), and the public 0.928-0.933 core and the 0.943 stack train this way, so k=12 is clearly not fatal. It was also forced by compute: Ortho at k=12 already takes 45 min/epoch on all data, and k=24 at 11 epochs (~16.5 h) does not fit an 11 h session without resume. What does NOT hold up is the Stage B change: it moved 54 -> 76-82 windows without revisiting k, which cut coverage per bag by a quarter. Nothing in the docs discusses that. (2) Was it already measured? No. Every summary.json has k=12, and the only bag-size number is the inference curve. WIN-PLAN:183 is right that an inference curve cannot price a training change. The curve still helps the mechanism argument: weights trained on 12-window bags lose 0.048 when they see only 12 evenly spaced windows. That shows a 12-window bag often lacks evidence the full bag has, which is the condition the training loss works under. (3) Is the cost overstated? Probably, for the headline framing. (a) Random instance subsampling in attention-MIL is a standard regularizer. Over 11-14 epochs each lesion still shows up in roughly 30-65% of steps, and a flexible head tends toward P(y|subset), which generalizes to full bags (the curve saturates by 36-54 windows). (b) Stage B gained +0.011 on the 691 despite sparser bags (confounded by 384 px, canonicalization, more slices and the LLRD package). (c) Of the four findings weak on gold, only Lateral Meniscus is truly focal. Lateral OA and PF OA are regional and visible across most coronal or axial windows, so their effective w is often 8-15 (miss 7-24%), not 2-6, and Synovitis is diffuse. (d) A final ensemble dilutes any single-model gain. (4) Did the project know and fix it? It knew: the brainstorm raised it, WIN-PLAN listed it as M1 and cut it on owner-hours. It never fixed or tested it. (5) Did AUDIT mis-close it? No. The AUDIT line was narrow and correct for what it addressed (count mismatch for a permutation-invariant pool). No later doc cites it to justify k=12, so 'mis-closed' overstates it. Net: the factual parts hold and the mechanism is plausible. But this is an untested, compute-constrained default, not a measured mistake, and its likely size is second-tier against a 0.026 gap.
fix: Step 0, decisive and cheap. Test whether the HEAD learns better from full bags, using the existing Ortho r1 weights (the 691 is clean: r1 trained on 3,502). Dump the LayerNorm'd per-window encoder features for every window of the 3,502 train and 691 val studies, ~76 x 1024 fp16 per study, ~650 MB in total. On the Mac, refit WindowMIL's head (norm/where/att/w/b) from one fixed init with r1's head lr, pos_weight and confidence weight, in two arms: k=12 random bags vs full bags. Run 2 seeds each and pair them on the 691 with score_oof. If full bags win, swap that head into the final Ortho last.pt: same keys, same inference code, no encoder retraining. This is the cheapest bankable piece. Step 1, end to end, only if Step 0 or the CNN arm is positive. Train with `--k 24 --micro 1`. Per-forward memory equals today's micro 2 x k 12 (24 windows: 14.5 GB Ortho with ckpt-12 + compile, 6.5 GB CoAtNet), so it is a flag change with no code. CoAtNet: ~65-70 min/epoch on 2xT4 DDP, 7 epochs fits one session. Ortho all-data: ~90 min/epoch, 11 epochs = ~16.5 h, which needs resume across two sessions (~50 lines) or a rented A100/H100 in bf16. k=36 for Ortho needs all-24-block checkpointing (est. ~10-11 GB at 36 windows by linear scaling of speed_bench_v2's 7.02 GB at 24; bench it, don't trust the extrapolation) and ~3.4x r1's time per epoch. Training on all ~76 windows end to end is not feasible on T4 within a session (~6-7x time). The full-bag alternative is to forward all windows and backprop through a subset, running the rest under no_grad (and in BN-eval mode for CoAtNet). That costs ~2.3x per epoch, the same order as k=24, and gives the head complete-evidence bags. Slot/depth-stratified k=12 is free but weak: the curve shows even evenly spaced 12 windows lose 0.048 at eval, so it fixes little. Do not shrink epochs to pay for a larger k without measuring it; that confounds the test.
expected_lb_gain: +0.000 to +0.005 on the final blend (single Ortho model up to ~+0.006), central guess ~+0.002. Mostly on Lateral Meniscus, MCL, Lateral OA and PF OA. Speculative: no training-side measurement exists in the repo. A head-only refit, if positive, is probably +0.001-0.003 of that.
gain_basis: For a gain: (a) hypergeometric miss rates at Stage B, k=12: 34% of positive bags miss a 6-window lesion and 50-71% miss a 2-4-window one. k=24 cuts the 6-window rate to 9%. (b) The curve shows a 12-window bag carries much less evidence than the full bag (−0.048 macro at eval on the same weights). (c) The weakest 691 findings (MCL 0.772, Lateral OA 0.777, PF OA 0.795) and the weakest gold findings include the regional/focal ones. (d) Each window gets only ~2 gradient passes per run (12/82 x 14). Against: (e) the frontier and stack cores train at k=12 and reach 0.928-0.943; (f) Stage B gained +0.011 on the 691 despite sparser bags; (g) random-subset MIL acts partly as regularization; (h) for OA findings w is large, so miss rates are low; (i) blending dilutes single-model gains, and on this project 691 gains have translated roughly 1:1 at best (Stage B +0.011 on the 691 -> +0.014 LB). The 691 paired SE between retrained models is ~0.003-0.0045, so a true single-model gain under ~+0.006 needs two seeds per arm to show. Toward 0.965 (a 0.026 gap) this is a second-tier lever, not a gap-closer.
